analysis:
The supplied units are CI/build/docs only: integration.yml, Makefile, a changelog fragment, and docs/README.md. None changes runtime authorization, attestation, encryption or billing code, and none touches TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011.

integration.yml: The exact-cache lane (head lines 290-291) adds DARKBLOOM_CBV2_KV_QUANTIZATION=native and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_CHECKPOINT_QUANTIZATION=native. The smoke lane (head 320-346) now expects paged and fails if either precision variable or DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PAGED_KV is set. No new secrets, triggers or permissions. HF_TOKEN is still limited to push events, with unauthenticated downloads on pull_request. Actions remain SHA-pinned.

Makefile: provider-test adds scripts/test-stage-swiftpm-resource-bundles.py (line 71). benchmark-wrapper-test adds three Python test runs, including reports/runtime-kv-path-2026-10-09/qualification/test_*.py (lines 83-85). These are local test invocations only. The referenced scripts are not in the supplied units, so I could not read them.

changelog.d/native-inference-quantized-checkpoints.md and docs/README.md: The changelog describes new lossy, bounded-CPU quantization of the encrypted SSD checkpoint rows, with layout/profile identities and a native fallback. This touches the T-041 surface (encrypted SSD prefix cache, A-001): at-rest metadata, AAD, layout identities, the KEK/HMAC lookup design and TTL. The implementing Swift sources (KVCacheSSD/SSDBlockStore.swift, SSDLookupKeys.swift) are not in this batch, so the integration pass should check:
- Whether the new layout/profile identity fields are plaintext AAD or metadata, and whether they add prompt-derived content beyond the keyed lookupTag.
- Whether the HMAC scope folding is unchanged.
- Whether restoring older rows or converting formats can bypass the salt, scope or weightHash bindings.
- Whether the T-041 detection_hint and mitigations need a documented update.

This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a defect.
